clips.text_zh: /biz/ 又有癲佬計數：如果 PONS 真係 flip 到 Pump.fun，可以殺到 $3。DOGE1 食到 1% DOGE 街貨已經 $150M market cap。又係 meme 配 stocks，boomer 直接入 crypto。望住個 chart 我又想 all-in，但又諗起上次 CFD 輸到阿媲都唔認 😭 命理叫我今日 hold 住先，唔好再加注。
clips.text_en_b1: How high can PONS and Doge actually go? I did the maths. If PONS flips Pump.fun, we could see PONS around $3. If DOGE1 captures just 1% of the real DOGE market cap, that is already a $150 million market cap. Pairing memes with stocks is wild. Boomers who already own stocks will be able to get into crypto with one click.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread about PONS and DOGE1 upside math

signal.rationale: OP lays out a concrete upside case for DOGE1 capturing 1% of DOGE market cap, implicitly bullish on DOGE-adjacent plays

clips.text_en_b2: Someone on /biz/ ran the numbers and the projections look genuinely wild. If PONS somehow manages to flip Pump.fun, we could realistically see PONS hitting around $3. Meanwhile, DOGE1 capturing just 1% of DOGE's market cap would already translate into roughly $150 million. Pairing meme tokens with traditional stocks is an unusual move, although it could let boomers pivot into crypto with a single click.
clips.text_en_c1: Should one really trust the deluded number-crunching on /biz/? Apparently, if PONS somehow managed to dethrone Pump.fun, its price could realistically approach three dollars. Meanwhile, DOGE1 absorbing merely one percent of DOGE's market capitalisation would translate into a valuation of roughly 150 million. The fusion of meme tokens with traditional equities is nothing short of absurd. Stock-holding boomers, who already navigate equities comfortably, could acquire cryptocurrency with a single click. Looking at the chart, half of me wants to go all-in; the other half remembers my CFD debacle last quarter. I think I'll heed the stars for once and simply hold my position rather than chasing further exposure.
clips.text_en_c2: A fresh round of speculative arithmetic has resurfaced on 4chan's /biz/, this time with PONS and DOGE1 in the crosshairs. Should PONS somehow succeed in flipping Pump.fun's valuation, a per-token figure in the vicinity of $3 appears mathematically plausible, while DOGE1 absorbing a mere 1% of Dogecoin's circulating market capitalisation would, by the poster's reckoning, translate into something approaching $150 million. The underlying thesis remains a familiar one: that the conflation of meme equities with traditional stock holdings could grant legacy investors seamless on-ramps into digital assets. Choreographed, perhaps, for the boomer cohort already overexposed to equities. Yet such charts invariably invite reckless conviction, and the writer confesses, with characteristic ambivalence, to being haunted by previous CFD misadventures. Astrology, mercifully, counsels restraint for the day.

clips.text_zh: SpaceX 又有 lockup 到期🙏 9月9號大約 319M 股解禁，即係 7% baseline pool 同 2.4% total shares。IPO 後第 90 日，第三輪 major release event。Musk 仔又嚟料，short 佢定 long 佢好？上次 TSLA earnings 我已經輸一鑊，依家真係唔敢亂動。Tommy 叫我睇 AP 質素先再入場，但我個倉已經頂唔順。
clips.text_en_b1: On September 9, 2026, around 319 million more SpaceX shares become eligible to sell. That is about 7% of the baseline pool and roughly 2.4% of total shares outstanding. It marks the 90th trading day since the IPO and the third major lockup release event. Watch for supply pressure around that date.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread tracking SpaceX IPO lockup release calendar

signal.rationale: Calendar item only, no actionable setup in the OP

clips.text_en_b2: Another SpaceX lockup expiry is approaching, and this one could shake things up. Around 319 million shares become eligible to sell on September 9, representing roughly 7% of the baseline pool and about 2.4% of total shares outstanding. It falls on the 90th trading day post-IPO, marking the third major release event. Supply pressure around that date could be significant, so I'm watching closely before deciding whether to short or go long.
clips.text_en_c1: Another SpaceX lockup expiry is approaching. On September 9th, approximately 319 million shares will become eligible for sale, representing roughly seven percent of the baseline pool and around 2.4 percent of total shares outstanding. This marks the ninetieth trading day following the IPO and constitutes the third major release event. Should one short the position or go long? My TSLA earnings misadventure still stings, so I am frankly hesitant to act. Tommy advised me to scrutinise the associated prospectus before committing any capital, but my portfolio can scarcely tolerate further volatility at this juncture.
clips.text_en_c2: Yet another lockup cliff has materialised for SpaceX, with approximately 319 million shares becoming tradeable on the ninth of September. That tranche constitutes in the order of 7% of the baseline pool and roughly 2.4% of total shares outstanding, falling precisely on the ninetieth trading day following the IPO and constituting the third major vesting event of this cycle. The implications for near-term supply pressure are, by any reasonable assessment, non-trivial, particularly given the inherent illiquidity of a stock that has only recently entered the public markets. The thread on /biz/ oscillates predictably between bearish conviction and opportunistic longing, with the author disavowing any directional bias after last quarter's Tesla earnings debacle. Prudence, presumably, shall prevail until prospectus-grade disclosure permits otherwise.

clips.text_zh: /g/ 有人問點解永遠有人叫人用 paid ChatGPT / Claude，話 paid 先睇到真正實力。但其實 Kimi、GLM、Qwen 已經做到 90% performance，價錢可能 10% 都唔使。Surveying 助理都好多人話俾錢買 AI 先穩陣，但工程牌我自己都考緊，真係冇咁多 budget。Dr. An 都叫我用 Qwen 寫嘢慳時間。
clips.text_en_b1: Have you noticed this type of post? 'If you have not tried the PAID models you do not know what they are capable of.' Why do you never see people telling others to spend a tiny fraction on a cheaper model like Kimi, GLM or Qwen, which gets you easily 90% of the performance for maybe 10% of the price?
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread about paid vs cheaper AI models

signal.rationale: General AI tooling discussion, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Have you noticed how /g/ is flooded with posts insisting you need to pay for ChatGPT or Claude to unlock their true potential? It is genuinely puzzling. Meanwhile, models like Kimi, GLM, and Qwen already deliver around 90% of that performance, often at a fraction of the cost. While premium tools certainly have their merits, many survey assistants still insist paid versions are the safer bet. I am juggling my engineering exams on a tight budget, so cheaper alternatives just make sense.
clips.text_en_c1: One frequently encounters posts asserting that anyone who has not tried paid ChatGPT or Claude has no genuine appreciation of their capabilities. Yet remarkably few advocate for cheaper alternatives such as Kimi, GLM, or Qwen, which arguably achieve ninety percent of the performance at perhaps ten percent of the price. Surveying assistants often insist that paid subscriptions are essential for reliability, but as someone currently pursuing engineering certifications, my budget simply cannot accommodate recurring AI costs. Dr. An recommended Qwen for streamlining documentation, and frankly, the value proposition is difficult to dispute.
clips.text_en_c2: A rhetorical pattern has grown irksome across the AI discourse: the insistent refrain that one cannot genuinely assess frontier capability without ponying up for ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions. The implicit suggestion is that the paid tier alone reveals what these systems can truly accomplish, while the open-weight alternatives remain consigned to permanent also-ran status. Yet Kimi, GLM and Qwen have demonstrably closed the gap to within striking distance of their proprietary counterparts, delivering what is colloquially termed ninety percent of the performance at a fraction, perhaps a tenth, of the cost. The economic calculus for an individual practitioner, particularly one juggling professional examinations on a constrained budget, renders the subscription gospel increasingly untenable. Subscriptions, after all, are recurrent; competence, once cultivated, compounds indefinitely.

clips.text_zh: 21 間美國銀行夾份推 stablecoin，Trump 已經將美國賣晒俾私人公司同 bank。即將會有 Apple Coin、Google Coin、Tesla Coin、X Coin、銀行幣⋯⋯美國金融市場會俾幾百種 digital cash 淹沒。我喺 HK 都睇到呢單新聞，李生都話 bitcoin 可能受惠。考牌溫書溫到頭都痛，睇下新聞抖下。
clips.text_en_b1: 21 U.S. banks plan to launch a joint stablecoin. This is the real purpose behind Trump's stablecoin bill. He has sold out the U.S. to private companies and banks, allowed them to issue their own currencies to sell government bonds. Soon there will be Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin, and Bank Coin everywhere.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread about US banks issuing a joint stablecoin

signal.rationale: News commentary on policy, no direct trade thesis in the OP

clips.text_en_b2: Twenty-one U.S. banks are joining forces to launch a joint stablecoin, and this could be the real endgame behind Trump's recent legislation. Critics argue he has effectively handed the country over to private corporations, since these entities can now mint their own currencies to sell government bonds. The market will soon be flooded with Apple Coin, Google Coin, Tesla Coin, and countless bank-issued tokens. Even from Hong Kong, the implications are impossible to ignore.
clips.text_en_c1: Twenty-one American banks have jointly agreed to launch a stablecoin, ostensibly fulfilling the underlying purpose of Trump's stablecoin legislation. Critics argue the administration has effectively outsourced America's monetary infrastructure to private corporations and financial institutions, permitting them to mint currencies for the purpose of offloading government debt. Within months, the financial ecosystem may well be inundated with hundreds of digital cash variants: Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin, and various bank-issued tokens. Even from Hong Kong, one can scarcely escape the headlines. Mr. Lee speculated that bitcoin might ultimately benefit.
clips.text_en_c2: A consortium of twenty-one American banking institutions has coalesced around a joint stablecoin initiative, ostensibly to facilitate the issuance of tokenised debt against the federal government's balance sheet. The political reading, articulated with characteristic bluntness on /pol/, contends that the relevant stablecoin legislation represents a wholesale transfer of monetary sovereignty to private enterprise, with incumbent banks acquiring de facto authority to mint parallel currencies. The downstream proliferation appears inevitable: Apple Coin, Google Coin, Microsoft Coin, Tesla Coin, X Coin, and a generic Bank Coin shall, presumably, compete for transactional primacy in a marketplace already saturated with dollar-pegged alternatives. From Hong Kong, where one observes such developments with professional detachment, the implications for Bitcoin's relative scarcity thesis appear decidedly favourable, even as the regulatory perimeter remains conspicuously undefined.

clips.text_en_c2: The tenth episode of 100 Girlfriends' third season has, at long last, dropped, and the animation community's anticipation has, predictably, reached fever pitch. clips.text_zh: /fit/ 巴打 18% bf，每日行 15k-20k steps 燒 500-800 kcal，再 cut 500 kcal 食物，total 1000 kcal deficit。但 4 個禮拜落嚟個 scale 完全唔郁。Progressive overload 做到肌肉大咗但脂肪冇減。每週平均 90k steps，佢自己都好迷惘。睇到我好有 feel，肥仔信成日笑我 body image 焦慮，其實佢都係。
clips.text_en_b1: I'm at 18% body fat and stuck. I walk 15k to 20k steps a day, burning 500 to 800 calories just from that. I also cut 500 calories of food. So that is a 1000 kcal deficit. I can keep progressive overload and my muscles are getting bigger and more visible.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread from anon struggling to lose fat on a 1000 kcal deficit

signal.rationale: Body recomp question, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: I am hovering around 18% body fat and completely plateaued despite running a serious deficit. Each day I log between 15k and 20k steps, burning anywhere from 500 to 800 calories through walking alone. On top of that, I trim roughly 500 calories from my diet, bringing the total daily deficit to around 1000 kcal. Progressive overload is working since my muscles are visibly growing, yet the scale refuses to budge after four solid weeks of consistency.
clips.text_en_c1: I find myself genuinely perplexed by this plateau. Currently hovering around eighteen percent body fat, I log between fifteen and twenty thousand steps daily, burning somewhere in the region of 500 to 800 calories from ambulation alone. Combined with a 500-calorie reduction in caloric intake, my aggregate deficit should approach 1000 kilocalories. Progressive overload remains consistent, and my musculature has grown noticeably more defined. Nevertheless, after four consecutive weeks, the scale refuses to budge, and subcutaneous fat appears stubbornly unchanged. Averaging roughly 90,000 steps weekly, I am beginning to wonder whether my methodology requires fundamental reassessment rather than mere incremental adjustment.
clips.text_en_c2: A poster on /fit/ finds himself in a metabolic quandary that would be familiar to any trainee caught between the competing demands of caloric restriction and progressive overload. Holding steady at approximately 18% body fat, he logs between fifteen and twenty thousand daily steps, expending somewhere in the region of five to eight hundred kilocalories through ambulatory activity alone, to which he adds a further five hundred kilocalorie dietary deficit for an aggregate daily shortfall exceeding one thousand kilocalories. The training stimulus has, by his account, yielded discernible muscular hypertrophy, with muscle groups becoming visibly more defined as the weeks accumulate. The bathroom scale, however, remains obstinately unmoved across four consecutive weeks, and the resulting disillusionment is palpable.

clips.text_zh: /a/ 又有膠文問 anime 漫畫入面，女角胸部到底幾大先算太大。巴打們又開始引戰 Gundam 00、鬼滅、進擊嘅巨人比例問題。望住個 thread 我笑咗出嚟，今晚溫書溫到悶當娛樂。Tommy 應該都鍾意睇呢啲膠討論。
clips.text_en_b1: When it comes to anime and manga busts, how big is too big? Anons on /a/ are debating the limits of character design proportions. The thread is full of comparisons between classic shows and modern designs, with no real consensus on where the line should be drawn.
clips.source_hint: /a/ discussion thread on anime bust size limits

signal.rationale: Anime character design banter, no trade relevance

clips.text_en_b2: Another day, another pointless thread on /a/ about anime bust proportions and where the line should actually be drawn. Anons are going back and forth, comparing classic series like Gundam 00 against modern hits such as Demon Slayer and Attack on Titan, debating which designs crossed the threshold. There is no real consensus, just endless flame wars over character silhouettes. Honestly, watching the thread unfold is far more entertaining than grinding through tonight's revision materials.
clips.text_en_c1: The eternal debate has resurfaced on /a/ regarding the upper limits of anatomical exaggeration in anime and manga character design. Specifically, contributors are dissecting precisely where proportionality crosses the threshold from stylistic flourish into outright absurdity. Comparisons range across established titles like Gundam 00, Demon Slayer, and Attack on Titan, with no discernible consensus emerging whatsoever. The thread devolves predictably into the customary Gundam versus contemporary aesthetic warfare that aficionados have witnessed countless times before. Honestly, watching the ensuing chaos provided welcome relief from an otherwise tedious evening of certification study.
clips.text_en_c2: The eternal question, resurrected once more on /a/, concerns the upper limits of mammary proportion within the medium of anime and manga, with the resident contrarians marshalling their customary array of comparative examples. Debates of this nature invariably devolve into partisan skirmishes over canonical franchises, with Gundam 00, Kimetsu no Yaiba, and Attack on Titan cited in alternating succession as either exemplars of restraint or harbingers of anatomical excess. The thread, predictably, has generated more heat than illumination, with participants ranging across stylistic eras in search of a definitive threshold. The absence of any genuine consensus is, of course, the entire point, and one observes the proceedings with the detached amusement afforded to those whose evening study sessions have grown insufferably tedious. Tommy, I suspect, would derive considerable pleasure from the spectacle.
